messages:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — Velora dedicated pool bring-up tomorrow 09:00 PT. Need final quota+autoscale profile signoff today.
Ajay Patel: Can you paste the expected steady qps and burst pattern? I want to validate quota headroom.
Maria Chen: Expected steady ~120 qps, 95th percentiles at ~180 during business hours, bursts up to 450 qps for short windows (30–90s).
Tom Ruiz: For those bursts do you expect many long-context requests? i.e., >1024 tokens? That changes batch sizing and GPU mem.
Maria Chen: Mostly short chat turns, <256 tokens. A few nightly batch jobs request embeddings for 50k rows — scheduled out of peak.
Sophie Nguyen: Ok I'll run a traffic profile that simulates steady + stochastic bursts. Which autoscale policy do we want live? simple_cpu_threshold or token-rate-based?
Ajay Patel: Prefer token-rate-based for cost predictability. Set min replicas=2, target per-replica throughput=150 qps, max replicas=20. Can we confirm warm-start behavior?
Tom Ruiz: Warm start: pool preloads model KV when replica spins up. We should set a 30s pre-warm window in the policy so the first tokens don't spike latency.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Also want a fallback model (quantized) if scale fails. Suggest rwd-small-quant as fallback.
Sophie Nguyen: I'll add the fallback rule: route to rwd-small-quant when estimated latency > 800ms for 60s.
Tom Ruiz: Load test checklist (quick):
```
- run k6 profile: steady-120 + poisson bursts
- validate p95 < 300ms steady, <800ms during burst
- monitor OOM and queue length
- validate KV cache hit > 90% for repeated prefixes
```
Ajay Patel: I'll own the quota signoff once the k6 results look good. Maria, can you share the customer enablement slot?
Maria Chen: Enablement session scheduled 10:30 PT tomorrow, 30m handoff + runbook walkthrough. Link: https://company.zoom/velora-enablement
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deployment for pool velora-dedicated at 2025-06-12T09:00:00Z — monitors: latency, errors, gpu_usage.
Sophie Nguyen: Plan for two dry-run load windows tonight at 22:00 and 02:00 PT. I'll drop results here.
Ajay Patel: Great. If the 22:00 run shows any p95 > 600ms we hold signoff and iterate.
Maria Chen: Thanks all — tagging @Sophie Nguyen @Tom Ruiz for final artifacts. I'll update the runbook after the second dry-run. :thumbsup:
